label: b8: entanneal, seed 3 of 4 — wave 1 of 2
notes: Batch b8 -- what fixes b4's collapse. Everything is held at b4's config: fc (200,100), 8 epochs, b2's reward function, PPO's defaults elsewhere, seeds 1-4 pinned to the arm letters. One knob moves per group of four. **b4 itself is the control** -- 8 seeds at this exact config -- so no control arms are queued; compare against b4 TRUNCATED TO 100M, since 65% of its >=98%/500 rows land after 100M and the full-run figure is not the right comparator. The effect being tested: past its competence onset b4 spends a median 9.1% of its evals below 50% perfect, against 0.7% for b6 (same network, 4 epochs) and 0.0% for b5 (fc 320, 8 epochs), and its >=98%/500 density is the worst of the three at 7.3%. 100M rather than b4's 200M because the drawdown rate is already 8.5% in the first 100M and 9.0% in the second -- the effect is fully developed by this cap, though it is invisible at 10M. Explore early, commit late: the same 0.01 b4 ran, ramped linearly to 0.001 over SNEK_MAX_STEPS. The schedule has existed since ppo/schedules.py landed and has never been used by an arm. It completes exactly at this cap, so the anneal and the budget are self-consistent.
